title: feat(spec): a field group lists its own members and order (fieldGroups[].fields)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuA3ABrP2TrxEXR2RauGGb9b)_

Fixes #35900

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: follow-up #35902

## 维护者速读

- 分组现在可以自己列出成员和顺序（`fieldGroups[].fields`）；写了它，分组里的字段按列表顺序显示，不再跟着对象的字段声明顺序走。
- 不写 `fields` 的对象完全不变：字段自己的 `group` 仍然有效，是旧写法，继续读取，不删除。
- 两种写法冲突时对象解析会拒绝（同一字段被两个分组列出、列表和字段自身 `group` 指向不同分组、同一列表重复、关联列表分组带 `fields`）；列了对象没有的字段只跳过，`os lint` 给警告。
- Studio 里在分组内拖动字段，只写这个分组的 `fields`，对象的字段顺序不动（列表视图的默认列顺序因此不受影响）。

## What changes

**Spec (`@objectstack/spec`)**
- `ObjectFieldGroupSchema` gains `fields?: string[]` (snake_case field names), the group's members in display order.
- `deriveFieldGroupLayout` (ADR-0085 §5, the single derivation the record page and both forms already read) now resolves membership through a new `readFieldGroupMembership(def)` export: listed names first in list order, first listing wins, names the object does not declare are skipped; then a field whose own `group` names a group (listing or not) that has not placed it yet, in declaration order (so a field whose `group` names a listing group that leaves it out is appended after the list); everything else goes to the trailing ungrouped bucket. Hidden fields are filtered as before.
- The object `superRefine` gains `refuseFieldGroupMembershipConflicts`: `fields` on a `relatedList` group; a name repeated in one list; a field listed by two groups (reported at the second listing); a listed field whose own `group` names a different group (reported at both places: `fieldGroups[i].fields[j]` and `fields.<name>.group`).
- `Field.group` docs now call it the older spelling of membership, still read.
- The object metadata form gains a `Fields` tags row in the field-group sub-form; translation bundles regenerated (zh-CN translated; other locales carry the source text as usual).
- Liveness ledger: `fieldGroups.children.fields` row (live). References docs, api-surface, authorable-surface, export-origins and state counts regenerated.

**Lint (`@objectstack/lint`)**
- New warning `field-group-member-unknown` for a listed name that is neither declared nor an injected platform column (an injected `owner_id` does not warn). Rules (b) and (d) count list members.

**Studio (`@object-ui/app-shell`)**
- `object-fields-io`: `groupMembership`, `currentGroupLayout` and `writeGroupLayout`. A drag writes only the groups whose order changed (as their `fields` lists) and drops a moved field's own `group` when it would contradict the list; the object's `fields` are written only when the ungrouped bucket (which has no list) is reordered, and then only among the bucket's own declaration slots.
- `ObjectFormDesigner`, `ObjectFormCanvas` (add, reorder, move by offset, move to group), `ObjectFieldInspector` (group select) and `ObjectGroupInspector` (member count; choosing a related list clears `fields`) read and write through those helpers. A drop that changes nothing writes nothing.
- AI-added fields stay visible: a field no list names still shows, through its own `group` or the ungrouped bucket.

Not touched on purpose: `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` and the form plugins (they already derive through `deriveFieldGroupLayout` and pass `fieldGroups` through), to stay clear of #35891 and #35889.

## Why

Epic #35896: tabs and field groups are declared on the parent. A group's order lived in the object's field declaration order, so reordering inside a section in Studio rewrote the whole `fields` map (and moved list-view default columns with it). The list makes the section own its order.

Seat claim readings (claim 7046434371, amended 7046460603): a listed name the object does not declare is skipped, not refused (deleting a field or an AI tool's edit never makes the object unparseable; lint warns); a field one list names while its own `group` names a different value is refused, and so is a repeat in one list; Studio drags write group `fields` lists while the ungrouped bucket still reorders declaration order.

## Tests

- `packages/spec/src/data/field-group-layout.test.ts`: derivation (list order, legacy beside list, append, skipped missing and hidden names, listed system field kept, empty list dropped, first listing wins, the membership helper) and parse (accepted forms and every refusal). 32 tests.
- `packages/spec/src/data/object-strictness-batch20.test.ts`: the pin that expected `fieldGroups[].fields` to be refused now accepts both spellings.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-semantic-roles.test.ts`: list members count as referenced / shadowed; unknown-name warning; injected `owner_id` raises none; a list naming only missing fields gets rules (b) and (e).
- `ui/.../object-fields-io.test.ts`: `writeGroupLayout` and `groupEntries`.
- Designer drag pins (`keyboardDrop-11871`, `keyboardGrid-11898`, `dndAnnouncements-11802`, `pinnedFields-27516`) now read the layout the draft resolves to. New: a reorder writes only `fieldGroups` and leaves `fields` the same object; a cross-group move lists the field and drops its `group`. Two expectations moved on purpose: a drop that changes nothing writes nothing, and Owner dropped onto Condition in a section lands after it and stays there after a reload.

## Acceptance notes

- No dedicated canvas test for `ObjectFormCanvas.addField` / `moveToGroup`; they share `writeGroupLayout`, which is covered directly.
- No browser run in this PR.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` on head 53409dca9: 866 files, 27813 passed, 1 todo, exit 0. (An earlier run had 2 failures, the batch20 pin and the metadata-form reconciliation; both are fixed above.)
- ESLint over the changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files: exit 0 (0 errors, 25 warnings).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test`: 9348 passed; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: exit 0 (after a full build).
- UI vitest for the five touched designer / io test files: all pass.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`: 123 commands, all exit 0 (four first answered exit 3 for missing build output or a shallow fixture commit and were re-run after `turbo run build` and fetching the fixture).
- `pnpm check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage`, `check:i18n-walk-parity`, `check:i18n-stale-fill`: exit 0.
